findings.title: Single reserved `review-gate` branch cannot route the arch/slice/tasks gates, which fire earlier in the cascade
findings.description:
TD-3 and the Technical Scope both say the gate status is "rout[ed] through the reserved `LIFECYCLE: review-gate` branch," which slice 240 placed (per 240 TD-4) between `LIFECYCLE: in-implementation` and `LIFECYCLE: complete-advance`. But the design's own boundary-signal table and walkthrough require the gates to fire at three *earlier* cascade points: `arch` in the `GUARD: no-active-slice` path (no active slice, before any `LIFECYCLE:` branch), `slice` at the `needs-tasks` state (design present, no tasks — the doc's walkthrough step 6), and `tasks` while the slice is `in-implementation` (task file exists, not complete). `getNext()` is a first-match early-return cascade, so a slice in `needs-tasks` or `in-implementation` returns at those branches and never reaches a gate branch positioned after `in-implementation`; a no-active-slice project never enters `LIFECYCLE:` branches at all.

The design does place the *evaluation* correctly ("at each boundary in `deriveSliceStatus()` + the no-active-slice path"), so the mechanism is salvageable — but the routing description ("fill **the** reserved `review-gate` branch") describes one insertion point where three additional, earlier ones are actually required. As written, an implementer could wire only the pre-advance case into the reserved branch and leave the `slice`/`tasks`/`arch` recommendations unreachable, silently failing the plan's "covering all four lifecycle boundaries." This needs an explicit mapping from each boundary's derived status to the concrete cascade branch that emits the `review`/`blocked` recommendation (needs-tasks branch, in-implementation branch, no-active-slice dispatch, and the reserved pre-advance slot).

findings.title: Arch requires the block rationale to name the parse failure; the design's parser conflation and rationale contract can't produce it
findings.description:
The architecture (§Technical Considerations, "File-read failure modes") states: "The rationale returned to the caller **names the parse failure explicitly**." This design, however, (a) rests on `parseFrontmatter` returning the identical `{ found: false, data: {} }` for a file-read error, an unclosed/missing frontmatter block, *and* a well-formed frontmatter that simply lacks a `verdict` key — which I confirmed is exactly what `frontmatterParser.ts` does (the `catch` and the no-closing-`---` path both return `empty`, and a found-but-`verdict`-less doc returns `found: true` with no `verdict`); and (b) TD-7's rationale contract only requires naming the review type (and, for `review-failed`, the verdict + threshold) — it never names a parse/read failure.

The design does satisfy the arch's *conservative* half — an unparseable file is never silently passed (it is `UNKNOWN` → `review_unknown_as`, default `fail`). But it cannot satisfy the *diagnostic* half: with the three causes collapsed into one `UNKNOWN`, the gate has no signal for "this file could not be read/parsed" versus "frontmatter present but no `verdict` field," so the required rationale text is not derivable. Fixing it is cheap — branch on `parseFrontmatter().found` (and/or keep the error distinction) to classify the `UNKNOWN` cause, and add "names the parse/read failure when that is the cause" to TD-7's rationale requirement — but as specified the requirement is left unmet.

findings.title: Recommendation strings are human sentences, while the arch and the doc itself describe `review`/`blocked` as the stable machine tokens runners route on
findings.description:
The architecture's gate branch returns `{ recommendation: "review", ... }` / `{ recommendation: "blocked", ... }`, and this doc's Integration Points list "the `review` / `blocked` recommendation vocabulary — the stable strings runners route on." Yet TD-7's concrete examples set `recommendation` to full sentences ("Review required before advancing", "Blocked: review verdict does not clear threshold"), and the walkthrough echoes the sentences in `cf next` output. If the machine token is meant to be `review`/`blocked` (matching the arch) with the sentences relegated to `rationale`, that should be stated; if the token itself becomes the sentence, the "stable strings runners route on" wording in the same document is wrong. Low impact because TD-7 defers exact strings to implementation and the `NextAction` shape is unchanged — but the intended routing token should be pinned down so slice 242 and the Amoeba/Squadron consumers route on a stable value.

Verified and not raised: the `parent` frontmatter correctly points to the slice-plan document (not the architecture); dependency direction is 241→240 with no inversion; the per-gate `threshold`-override retention is explicitly authorized by both the plan ("241's design decides whether to keep it") and the arch's per-transition-override design, so it is not dead config; the `STATUS` const scope matches maintenance slice 910's entry verbatim; and the gating-off "byte-for-byte identical" guarantee is structural (optional ctor dep, no config read when off) with a named regression test.

structured_findings.summary: Single reserved `review-gate` branch cannot route the arch/slice/tasks gates, which fire earlier in the cascade
Arch requires the block rationale to name the parse failure; the design's parser conflation and rationale contract can't produce it
Recommendation strings are human sentences, while the arch and the doc itself describe `review`/`blocked` as the stable machine tokens runners route on
